value.body: Under the Agnipath scheme, launched in 2022, the Army, Navy and Air Force recruit soldiers, sailors and airmen below officer rank as Agniveers for a fixed four-year term, including training. At the end of each batch's term, up to a quarter can be selected for regular service; the rest leave with a lump-sum Seva Nidhi package. It is the main route into the ranks of the armed forces after Class 10 or 12.

items.label: Retention
items.note: Selected on merit for regular service

items.label: Age at entry
items.note: As set at launch; check each notification

items.label: Seva Nidhi at exit
items.note: Tax-free; about half is the Agniveer's own contribution
items.source: Ministry of Defence, scheme launch (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Each service runs its own process. Army: an online Common Entrance Exam, then a recruitment rally with physical fitness and measurement tests and a medical; categories include General Duty (Class 10), Technical (Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Maths) and Clerk / Store Keeper (Class 12). Air Force (Agniveervayu): Class 12 with Maths, Physics and English for science subjects, or other streams for non-science posts; an online test, physical fitness and adaptability tests, and a medical. Navy: Agniveer SSR needs Class 12 with Maths and Physics; selection is an online test, a physical fitness test and a medical.

value.title: At a glance
items: Most Agniveers leave after four years, so it helps to plan the next step — a degree, CAPF or police recruitment, or a skilled job.
Physical and medical standards are strict and differ by service and category.
Notifications, eligibility and age limits change by year; read each one in full.
Officer entry is a separate route (for example NDA after Class 12).
